$comment: Curated sector labels, beamline descriptions, techniques and 2026 status wording applied to research/sectors.json. Published references, directory URLs, station identifiers and enhancement delivery records are preserved. Display headings use sentence case. Enhancement text distinguishes the design from installed equipment and public confirmation.

1.plainLabel: High-energy X-rays in metals and batteries

enhancement.text: 1-ID uses X-rays at about 40 to 140 keV to measure stress and crystal grains through centimetres of metal. A keV is a thousand electron-volts. The upgrade plan replaces the bent-silicon-crystal monochromator, which selects one X-ray energy, with a horizontally deflecting version. This avoids blurring the smaller vertical source and adds a sample-handling and detector system at 1-ID-C. In 2026, the 1-ID-C system has been delivered and 1-ID-E retains its old setup. Installation of the new monochromator and planned superconducting undulator is not confirmed.

1.operators: XSD Optics at 1-BM; XSD Materials Physics & Engineering at 1-ID

1-BM-B,C.title: 1-BM-B,C: Optics and detector testing
1-BM-B,C.summary: Tests X-ray mirrors, lenses and detectors for APS and outside users.

1-ID-B,C,E.title: 1-ID-B,C,E: High-energy X-ray scattering
1-ID-B,C,E.summary: High-energy X-rays penetrate metal parts and batteries to measure stress and map crystal grains in 3D.

2.plainLabel: Element maps of cells, soils and chips

enhancement.text: 2-ID scans small X-ray spots across samples to map elements. Each element emits fluorescence at characteristic energies. The plan adds a mirror to each branch to image the source onto a fixed aperture, reducing sensitivity to the 2.5-fold vertical source-size change between operating modes. It replaces 2-ID-E zone plates with Kirkpatrick–Baez mirrors, raising transmission from 10 to 20% to 60 to 80%, and builds Bionanoprobe-II for frozen samples with a 10 nm resolution goal. In 2026, Bionanoprobe-II is under construction and 2-ID-E still uses zone plates.

2-ID-E.title: 2-ID-E: X-ray fluorescence microprobe
2-ID-E.summary: Maps elements in biological and environmental samples at sub-micrometre resolution.

2-BM-A,B.title: 2-BM-A,B: Microtomography
2-BM-A,B.summary: Records rapid 3D X-ray scans of rocks, batteries, insects and other samples during changes.

2-ID-D.title: 2-ID-D: X-ray microfluorescence and Bionanoprobe
2-ID-D.summary: Scans a 50 to 200 nm X-ray spot to map trace metals inside frozen cells and materials.

2.operators: XSD Imaging at 2-BM; XSD Microscopy at 2-ID

enhancement.text: 3-ID selects X-rays within about 0.001 eV out of 14,400 eV, better than one part in ten million. These excite nuclei of selected isotopes, including iron-57, to measure atomic vibrations in enzymes or samples under pressure. New Kirkpatrick–Baez focusing mirrors reduce the spot from about 20 µm toward 1 µm for diamond-anvil cells. In 2026, the iron-57 monochromator provides a 1.5 × 12 µm horizontal × vertical spot. A planned cryogenic monochromator depends on funding, and installation is not confirmed.

3-ID-B,C,D.title: 3-ID-B,C,D: Nuclear resonant scattering
3-ID-B,C,D.summary: Excites selected atomic nuclei to measure vibrations and magnetism, including at deep-Earth pressures. The nuclei include ⁵⁷Fe, ⁸³Kr, ¹⁵¹Eu and ¹⁶¹Dy.
techniques: Nuclear resonant scattering, NRIXS/NRVS, NFS and synchrotron Mössbauer

3.operators: XSD Inelastic X-ray & Nuclear Resonant Scattering

5.plainLabel: DND-CAT powder, surface and small-angle scattering

enhancement.text: DND-CAT operates 5-ID for powder diffraction, surface studies and small-angle scattering. Its 1995 mirrors had lost shape accuracy and reflectivity, and its silicon-crystal monochromator selected energies only up to 18 keV. The plan refurbishes the mirrors and upgrades the monochromator for a steadier, higher-energy beam. In 2026, the listed energy range reaches 35 keV, consistent with the monochromator upgrade. The mirror work has not been described publicly.

5-BM-B.title: 5-BM-B: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and diffraction
5-BM-B.summary: Measures X-ray absorption and diffraction in catalysts and materials during reactions.

5-ID-B,C,D.title: 5-ID-B,C,D: Powder diffraction, surface science and small-angle scattering
5-ID-B,C,D.summary: Three stations study powder structures, surface chemistry and small-angle scattering from polymers and nanomaterials.
techniques: Collaborative X-ray standing-wave and surface studies

6.plainLabel: Magnetism and atomic order in crystals

enhancement.text: Sector 6 studies magnetism and atomic order in crystals. Two undulators angled 1 milliradian apart now feed independent beams, for simultaneous operation of 6-ID-B/C and 6-ID-D. The plan adds compound refractive lenses, stacks of weak lenses, made from beryllium for a sub-micrometre focus at 6-ID-B/C and aluminium for high-energy 6-ID-D. A 60 keV test produced a 50 × 3.7 µm spot. Both beams are in user operation in 2026, with permanent-magnet devices instead of the planned superconducting undulator. Lens installation has not been announced.

6.operators: XSD Magnetic Materials at 6-ID; NSF SEES and XSD Materials Physics & Engineering at 6-BM

6-BM-A,B.title: 6-BM-A,B: Energy-dispersive diffraction and large-volume high-pressure experiments
6-BM-A,B.summary: Broad-energy X-rays measure strain in large engineering parts at station A and minerals under pressure at station B.
techniques: Energy-dispersive diffraction with a 20 to 200 keV white beam

6-ID-B,C.title: 6-ID-B,C: Resonant and magnetic scattering
6-ID-B,C.summary: Studies magnetic and electronic order in crystals, including under strong magnetic fields.
techniques: Diffraction in fields of 4 T static or about 30 T pulsed

6-ID-D.title: 6-ID-D: High-energy scattering
6-ID-D.summary: Measures diffuse X-ray scattering to study disorder in single crystals and liquids.

enhancement.text: 7-ID measures rapid changes by starting a reaction with a laser pulse and probing it after a controlled delay with an X-ray pulse. The upgrade added a first mirror to reduce heat on the monochromator and fixed-shape Kirkpatrick–Baez mirrors for a focus of about 100 nm. A dedicated 7-ID-D hutch supports time-resolved nanodiffraction with goals of 100 nm spatial and 100 ps temporal resolution. A picosecond is a trillionth of a second. The enhancement is delivered, and the general user program has fully resumed in 2026.

7-ID-B,C,D.title: 7-ID-B,C,D: Time-resolved diffraction and scattering
7-ID-B,C,D.summary: A laser pulse triggers a change, and delayed X-ray pulses measure atomic motion down to about a tenth of a billionth of a second.
techniques: Time-resolved nanodiffraction and multimodal imaging at 7-ID-D

8-BM-B.summary: Maps metals across whole tissue sections and samples up to about 10 cm across at micrometre resolution.

11.plainLabel: Atomic structure in glasses, catalysts and batteries

enhancement.text: Sector 11 measures atomic structure in glasses, catalysts and batteries with high-energy X-rays, including during reactions. The upgrade added two independent beams from undulators angled apart. It extended a new 11-ID-D station by 11 m, allowing a detector 12 to 15 m from the sample to measure atomic separations and nanoparticle sizes together. In 2026, 11-ID-B and 11-ID-C are in user operation and 11-ID-D is in scientific commissioning. Permanent-magnet undulators remain in use instead of the planned superconducting devices.

11-ID-C.title: 11-ID-C: High-energy X-ray scattering
11-ID-C.summary: Uses high-energy diffraction to study crystalline and amorphous materials in varied sample environments.

11-BM-B.summary: Measures high-resolution powder diffraction. Users can mail in samples.
techniques: High-resolution powder diffraction with 12 analyzers; mail-in samples

11-ID-B.title: 11-ID-B: Total scattering and powder diffraction
11-ID-B.summary: Measures atomic separations in glasses, liquids and nanomaterials, including during reactions.
techniques: Total scattering and PDF at 59 and 87 keV

11-ID-D.summary: An extended station measures structure from atomic bonds to nanoparticle dimensions in one experiment.
techniques: High-energy total scattering and SAXS, q from 0.01 to 40 Å⁻¹
Energy range from 26 or 30 keV to 130 keV

enhancement.text: Sector 12 measures particle sizes and shapes from about a nanometre to tens of micrometres using small-angle X-ray scattering, or SAXS. The upgrade added a long vacuum flight tube and lenses that focus onto a distant detector. These were designed to resolve angles up to about ten times finer. The ultra-small-angle instrument, USAXS, also moved from 9-ID and was rebuilt. The work is delivered in 2026 at the station now called 12-ID-E, with a 10 m flight tube rather than the planned 12 m.

12-BM-B.summary: Combines X-ray absorption with small-angle and wide-angle scattering on the same sample.

12-ID-E.summary: Uses ultra-small-angle scattering to measure structures from about a nanometre to tens of micrometres.
techniques: Pinhole SAXS with a 10 m path

13.plainLabel: GSECARS Earth science at high pressure

enhancement.text: GSECARS at the University of Chicago studies rocks, minerals and soils, including at deep-Earth pressures in diamond-anvil cells. The upgrade re-polished Kirkpatrick–Baez mirrors up to a metre long and added new mirrors to focus the smaller source accurately. It also upgraded a monochromator and stabilized instrument tables. The work was completed in 2025. In 2026, the 13-ID-E microprobe delivers about five times more flux, around 10¹³ photons per second, into a sub-micrometre spot.

15.plainLabel: ChemMatCARS liquid surfaces and small crystals

enhancement.text: ChemMatCARS, supported by the US National Science Foundation, studies liquid surfaces and small-crystal structures. The APS-U plan replaces an ageing electrically bent bimorph mirror and flat mirror with mechanically bent silicon mirrors. It adds 95 aluminium lenses for 30 to 70 keV beams with spots about 2 to 3 µm tall and 11 to 16 µm wide. NSF separately funded a second beamline at 15-ID-B and 15-ID-E. This beamline is in technical commissioning in 2026. Installation of the APS-U mirrors and lenses is not publicly confirmed.

25.plainLabel: Chemical-state maps and X-ray Raman scattering

enhancement.text: Sector 25 houses spectroscopy and time-resolved experiments. Two undulators placed one behind the other and angled apart feed independent beams for micro-spectroscopy and for laser-triggered experiments and X-ray Raman scattering. Raman scattering uses penetrating hard X-rays to study light elements. The enhancement funded liquid-nitrogen-cooled monochromators that select 4 to 40 keV with silicon crystals or a broader energy band with multilayers. The broader band passes 10 to 100 times more photons. An upgraded Raman spectrometer was also funded. The beamlines are in user operation in 2026; the new Raman instrument remains in commissioning.

25-ID-D,E.summary: Station D uses hard X-rays for Raman measurements of light elements usually studied with soft X-rays. Station E follows chemical changes with laser-pump and X-ray-probe measurements.

techniques: X-ray Raman scattering with LERIX at D
Time-resolved XAS, XES and scattering at E, from 200 to 300 ps resolution through 1 ms

techniques: X-ray emission with miniXS and multi-element von Hamos

25.operators: XSD Spectroscopy at 25-ID-C and 25-ID-D; XSD Time-Resolved Research at 25-ID-E

26.plainLabel: Strain and chemistry with a 20 nm X-ray spot

enhancement.text: The Hard X-ray Nanoprobe at 26-ID-C maps strain and chemistry with a 20 nm spot. It is operated by the Center for Nanoscale Materials and APS. The plan rebuilds the microscope to scan a roughly 1 µm square field at about 10 nm resolution in 10 to 100 milliseconds and adds laser-triggered measurements. It also refurbishes the first mirror, rebuilds the monochromator for about 100 times more heat, and adds 15 to 25 keV zone plates. The beamline accepts users in 2026, but the rebuilt microscope and new lenses are not publicly confirmed.

26.operators: Center for Nanoscale Materials with XSD Microscopy

27.plainLabel: Electronic and magnetic excitations in quantum materials

enhancement.text: 27-ID measures electronic and magnetic excitations in quantum materials by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering, or RIXS. This resolves small energy losses as X-rays excite the material. Some spectrometer stages were over 30 years old, and their rotation axes met within about 200 µm. The rebuild targeted a 5 µm tolerance, separated sample motion from the detector arm, and added room for larger sample environments. It was the first APS-U enhancement completed, in March 2022, before the old ring shut down.

enhancement.text: 30-ID measures phonons, collective atomic vibrations in crystals, with an energy resolution of about 1 to 1.5 meV at 23,700 eV. A meV is a thousandth of an electron-volt; this resolution is about one part in 16 to 24 million. The plan cools high-resolution monochromator crystals to reduce energy drift. A 3-ID test held drift near 0.05 meV over three to four days, more than 100 times steadier than before. In 2026, the first high-heat-load monochromator is listed as cryogenically cooled. Operation of the new high-resolution monochromator is not confirmed.

techniques: HERIX phonon measurements at 23.7 keV with meV resolution at C

32.plainLabel: Ultrafast X-ray imaging and nanoscale 3D scans

enhancement.text: 32-ID records rapid events, including laser melting in 3D printing, with X-ray pulses about 100 ps long. Its transmission X-ray microscope also produces nanoscale 3D images. The upgrade angled the two undulators apart and moved the microscope to 32-ID-B. The plan uses one beam for imaging and a second, focused by lenses and redirected by multilayer mirrors, for simultaneous diffraction at the same spot. In 2026, the angled beams and relocated microscope are in use, and 32-ID-C offers second-beam high-speed diffraction. The simultaneous setup and a planned projection microscope for nanoscale CT are not confirmed.
